proposition: A Mokobara Transit Backpack is the one thing a man with nothing left still has, and thirty litres of it is enough to carry a way home.

board.style_line: Photoreal live-action, vertical 9:16, 40mm, handheld-steady on a static head, one low-sun key off the water, bleached driftwood-grey grade with a single saturated accent, natural unretouched skin and salt, shallow-but-not-creamy depth, no stylisation, no colour pops other than the one named.
board.negative_line: no text, no logos, no watermarks, no captions, no subtitles, no signage, no letterforms or numbers of any kind, no brand marks, no celebrity or actor likeness, no film-poster styling, no title-card look, no ships, no crew, no other people, no modern vessels or aircraft, no weapon pointed at camera, no blood, no CGI gloss, no lens flare, no colour grading toward teal-and-orange, no extra limbs or malformed hands.

identity_anchors.transit_backpack: deep navy matte body; bright yellow lining; vertical front zip and front bucket pocket with two black zip pulls; black padded straps, small top grab handle
identity_anchors.castaway: one man in his forties, South Asian, sun-scorched and thin, uncut hair tied back with cord, unstyled beard, salt-stiffened ragged cotton shirt and rolled trousers, barefoot, hands cracked
identity_anchors.island: a small uninhabited shore of black basalt and pale sand, bleached driftwood and low dry scrub, flat open sea to the horizon, no structures and no boats

hero_frame.description: Three-quarter rear, camera at thigh height in ankle-deep water: he wades out toward the driftwood raft with the Transit Backpack high on his back. In one still you can see the deep navy matte body, both black zip pulls, both black padded straps over his shoulders, the small top grab handle standing up with the carved spear-shaft lashed flat beneath it, and a finger-width of bright yellow lining at the open top pocket. His shirt is rags, the raft is grey, the sand is bleached, the rope is frayed — the pack is the only dark, intact, dry-looking object anywhere in the frame.

audio.music_bed: None for the first 19.5 s. From 19.5 s, one low sustained string, no melody and no percussion, entering under the straps taking weight and decaying into surf across the brand card without resolving. The bed never rises above the surf.

beats.title: The tally
beats.feeling: The worn-flat patience of a man who stopped expecting anything, and the viewer's low unease at not being told what is being counted.
beats.framing: Static, camera at waist height, 40mm. Lower two-thirds: a slab of wet black basalt, ragged columns of scratched tally marks running off both frame edges. A sun-cracked hand enters from frame right at the lower third and drags a shell edge down the rock in one long stroke, cutting a fresh mark. Top third: flat open sea and a low sun just above the horizon, camera-left. His face is not in frame at any point. The only movement is the hand and a thin sheet of water sliding back down the rock.
beats.first_frame: The shell is held against the rock at the start of the stroke and the new mark is not cut yet; the hundreds of older marks are already there, some weathered smooth, some fresh. In the soft sand at bottom-right, out of focus, one black zip pull and a finger-width of deep navy fabric sit half-buried — the only manufactured object anywhere in the frame.
beats.impact: No cut and no camera move for the full 5 s; the shot holds exactly as long as it takes to say aloud what is in it. Sound: surf under everything from the first frame, then one long dry scratch of shell on stone that finishes on the last frame. No music. The frame gives the viewer two things to find and answers neither.

beats.title: What the tide gives back
beats.feeling: Recognition arriving a half-second before hope does — the small physical shock of seeing something that belongs to your old life.
beats.framing: Static wide, camera set low in the sand, 28mm, sea to the horizon across the top third, the same low sun still camera-left. The man is small and left of centre, crouched at the tally rock with the shell still in his hand. A wave runs up the beach and recedes, stripping the sand off the backpack in the lower-right third: deep navy matte body, both black zip pulls, the padded straps folded under it, the grab handle flat. He stops mid-stroke and turns his head toward it. Nothing else in the frame moves.
beats.first_frame: The wave at its furthest reach up the sand, water sheeting, the sand still smooth and the pack still completely buried — the frame looks like an ordinary wide of an empty beach and announces nothing.
beats.impact: The reveal is done by the water, not by the man and not by the camera; the camera never moves and he never walks toward it inside this beat. Sound: the drag of the wave pulling back, and inside that drag one wet, specific sound of nylon coming free of sand. Still no music. The cut out of beat 1 is motivated by the wave arriving in the outgoing frame's sound.

beats.title: What was still inside
beats.feeling: The private ache of being expected home, cut short by the man himself — the beat turns into a decision before it can become grief.
beats.framing: Tight over-shoulder, 50mm, camera just above the pack, sand and his knees filling the bottom of the frame. His hands run the vertical front zip open in one pull and the bright yellow lining flares against the deep navy — the first saturated colour anywhere in the film. Inside, dry: a folded tarp, a coil of cord, a folding knife, a fire-steel, and a small photograph. He lifts the photograph into the lower-left third; his wife's face is legible, the printing on its reverse is not. He looks at it for two beats, turns it face-down on his knee, and his hand goes straight back into the bag.
beats.first_frame: The bag shut and upright on the sand, wet navy with sand still in the seams, the small grab handle standing up, both black zip pulls together at the bottom of the vertical zip — one second before any yellow exists in this film.
beats.impact: The zip's full run is the sound of the beat, mixed loud and clean against the surf; with no voice anywhere in the film the ear takes it as a statement. No push-in — the camera holds while the hands do all of it. The photograph is never turned to camera and never lingered on. Supplied Mokobara wordmark composites low-centre from 9.5 s, inside the ten-second gate, on a frame where the product is doing something rather than posing.

beats.title: Everything he owns
beats.feeling: The dry pleasure of watching something take one more thing than it should — a smile, not a laugh, and never at the man's expense.
beats.framing: One static three-quarter-front shot, 35mm, camera at sand height. The pack stands upright centre-right in the lower two-thirds, sea and low sun across the top third. Laid out in a single countable row on the sand in front of it: a carved wooden spear-shaft, a coil of hand-knotted net, the fire-steel, a bundle of dried fish, four coconuts. In one unbroken take his hands feed all of it into the front bucket pocket, the last coconut going in with a shove from the heel of his hand. Then the vertical front zip closes in one clean pull, both black pulls meeting at the top. He lashes the spear-shaft flat under the small top grab handle, lying along the pack and pointing away from camera.
beats.first_frame: The empty bucket pocket held open by one hand with yellow showing at its mouth, and the whole load lying in a row on the sand in front of it — the viewer can count the coconuts before anything has moved.
beats.impact: The longest hold in the film because it is the busiest frame; no cutaway, no reaction shot, no comic sting in the track. The joke is carried entirely by the inventory being countable first and the zip closing cleanly at the end — he stays deliberate throughout and never looks at the lens. 'Transit Backpack' and '30L' composite in the lower third on the exact frame where the last coconut goes in, so the capacity figure arrives at the instant the viewer decides whether to believe the load.

beats.title: Shouldering it
beats.feeling: Steadiness. A man who has stopped counting and started carrying — the relief of having a plan, not the thrill of escape.
beats.framing: Three-quarter rear, camera at thigh height in ankle-deep water, 50mm, the low sun now ahead of him rather than camera-left. He wades out toward a lashed driftwood raft in the mid-ground. The pack rides high on his back: navy body, both black zip pulls, both padded straps on his shoulders, the small grab handle upright with the spear-shaft lashed flat beneath it, a finger of yellow lining showing at the open top pocket. His shirt is rags, the raft is grey, the sand is bleached; the pack is the only dark, intact, dry-looking thing in frame. The camera pans about four degrees right to hold him and stops when he stops.
beats.first_frame: His back at the waterline, the pack already settled and the straps already taking weight, the first step not yet taken; the raft small ahead of him and the edge of the tally rock just leaving frame behind his shoulder — the count and the way out in the same still.
beats.impact: This is the frame that sells the bag with no words: everything a man owned on this island has failed except this one object, and he is wearing it into the sea. The pan is motivated by his walk and by nothing else. Sound: water at his thighs, rope creak from the raft, the small leather-and-webbing sound of straps taking load. The single low string enters here — the first music in the film, after the feeling has already been made by four beats without any.

beats.title: Pushing off
beats.feeling: Release. The count is over and nothing is said about it.
beats.framing: Static wide from the beach, 28mm, the raft small and low in the frame, open sea and sky filling the top two-thirds, the sun low ahead. He plants a pole in the sand bar and pushes; the raft slides left-to-right, the same direction he has travelled since beat 2. The navy pack sits upright and lashed in the bow, unmistakable at that size because the yellow was set on it in close-up fourteen seconds earlier. There is no land ahead of him in frame.
beats.first_frame: The pole planted, the raft still touching bottom, the pack already lashed upright in the bow and his weight not yet committed — nothing has moved yet and the sea ahead is empty to the horizon.
beats.impact: Held long enough that the raft genuinely leaves part of the frame rather than being cut away from. The tally rock is never shown again. Sound: pole grinding on sand, water, the string holding underneath. Screen direction is unbroken from beat 2, so no bridging shot is needed.

beats.title: Brand close (composed by code)
beats.feeling: Quiet arrival. Nothing is sold at the viewer; the object is simply left on screen.
beats.framing: Composed by code, not generated. The last generated frame of beat 6 is held and graded down two stops as a ground. Over it, in the lower two-thirds, a still product plate of the Transit Backpack in the private-island colourway, three-quarter front on wet sand — deep navy matte body, bright yellow lining showing a finger's width at the top, vertical front zip and front bucket pocket with both black zip pulls, black padded straps, small top grab handle. Supplied Mokobara wordmark SVG, unaltered, in the upper third; 'mokobara.com' set beneath the wordmark.
beats.first_frame: The pack alone, upright on wet sand with the sea behind it — the same object the film has followed for thirty seconds, now still.
beats.impact: No motion, no whip-in, no music sting: the sustained string from beat 5 decays into surf and stops. The last thing on screen is the product, and the only words on it are the three the customer supplied.

name_and_size.why: Lands on the frame where the last coconut goes into the bucket pocket. The name identifies what has just performed and the figure is the specific fact the exaggeration is standing on, arriving at the exact second the viewer is deciding whether to believe the load. Placed in the lower third, off-centre left, over flat wet sand so the ground under the letters is even and dark; set in the brand's own grotesque, mixed case, weight medium, well above the large-text size floor, measured against the darkest and lightest sand pixels under the letters.

close_card.why: The ask, made once and only at the end, under the supplied wordmark on the composed brand card. It sits on a graded-down still ground rather than over moving water, so the contrast is fixed and measurable, and it is the only place in the film where the viewer is asked to do anything.

mandatory.customer_words: lets make an ad with mokobara
mandatory.realisation: The Mokobara Transit Backpack in the private-island colourway is the subject of the film, not a prop in it: it is planted in frame one, opened in close-up at 9.5 s, performs at 14-19.5 s, is worn in the hero frame, is carried out to sea, and is the last image on screen. The supplied wordmark and mokobara.com are the only brand marks used, both composited from the supplied files.

mandatory.customer_words: i would preferably give it the odysey movie angel
mandatory.realisation: The film runs on the myth's shape rather than any film's surface: a man held years from home on an island, the sea as the obstacle, a wife waiting, a homeward departure. Beat 1's tally wall and beat 6's lone raft carry that register without any named work, character, vessel, title card or score.

The bag is established as already his and from before: it is weathered, sand-packed and half-buried in frame one, and what is inside it at beat 3 — his wife's photograph, his own tarp, cord, knife and fire-steel — is a life he packed himself, not a supply drop.

mandatory.customer_words: the protagonist found his mokobara bag, while he was on the island where he was kept for years
mandatory.realisation: The find happens on the island and the years are shown rather than stated: hundreds of tally marks on wet basalt in beat 1, of which he is cutting one more. The receding wave uncovers the bag in beat 2 and he stops mid-stroke.

mandatory.customer_words: in that bag he founds her wives photo
mandatory.realisation: Beat 3: the zip runs open on the yellow lining, and among the dry contents is a small photograph of his wife. He lifts it into the lower-left of frame, holds it for two beats and turns it face-down on his knee — the emotional turn of the film, played as a decision.

mandatory.customer_words: and a lot of stuff that he could use to go back
mandatory.realisation: The bag's contents at beat 3 are all usable and all visible: a folded tarp, a coil of cord, a folding knife and a fire-steel. The cord is what lashes the driftwood raft that appears in beat 5, so the kit visibly becomes the way home rather than being described as one.

mandatory.customer_words: he packs food and stuff and goes back
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4 is the packing, in one unbroken take: dried fish and four coconuts as the food, plus the spear-shaft, the net and the fire-steel. Beat 5 is the shouldering, beat 6 the push-off, with no land ahead of him in frame.

mandatory.customer_words: would be funny that he could keep his arms in the bag and food and so much stuff
mandatory.realisation: The comic beat, kept to one static shot and played dry. The whole load lies in a countable row on the sand, the front bucket pocket takes every item including a last coconut shoved in with the heel of his hand, and the vertical zip still closes in one clean pull. His 'arms' are the carved spear-shaft, which goes in and is then lashed flat under the grab handle. He never mugs, nothing falls out, and the capacity figure supers on the frame that asks to be believed.

mandatory.customer_words: Avoid getting copyright violoations from odysssey
mandatory.realisation: Declared as a production rule and carried in the negative line: no named work, no title card, no character name, no actor likeness or key-art styling, no ship, no crew, no suitors, no cyclops, no bow, no orchestral hero theme. The only borrowings are tally marks, a lashed driftwood raft and a photograph — motifs no one owns — and the castaway's look is specified independently (South Asian, forties, unstyled beard) so it cannot converge on any released film's lead.

One vertical 9:16 film, exactly 30.0 s, seven contiguous beats of which six are generated shots and the seventh is a code-composed brand close. The vertical frame is used rather than merely filled: every beat opposes an element at the top of the long axis against one at the bottom.

mandatory.customer_words: "identity_invariants": ["deep navy matte body", "bright yellow lining", "vertical front zip and front bucket pocket with two black zip pulls", "black padded straps, small top grab handle"]
mandatory.realisation: All four are restated verbatim in the identity anchor carried in every prompt, and all four are visible together in the hero frame. Each is also given its own moment: the navy body half-buried in beat 1 and wet in beat 2, the yellow lining flaring at beat 3, the bucket pocket and both zip pulls performing at beat 4, the padded straps and grab handle at beat 5. The reference product asset transit_backpack_private_island_1 conditions every still so the likeness is the real product.

All three appear, verbatim and unreflowed, as overlays composited by code: name and capacity at 17.6-19.5 s, the url on the closing card at 28.0-30.0 s. No string is added, and no prompt quotes any word, so no letterform in the film is generated.

The audience is named by more than one variable: urban and metro Indian adults, roughly 25-40, who already buy in this price band and travel for work — not 'India'. The copy is originated in English for that reader rather than translated, the castaway is cast South Asian, and no Devanagari glyph is generated anywhere. Every claim is limited to the capacity figure, which is a product fact; ASCI code review sits outside Canon and is flagged for the customer.

brand_timeline.in_context: The product itself is in frame from 0.0 s — a black zip pull and a finger of navy half-buried in the sand behind his hand — and never lapses after that: wet and uncovered from 5.0 s, opened at 9.5 s, performing from 14.0 s, worn from 19.5 s, lashed in the bow from 24.0 s and alone on screen from 28.0 s. The supplied Mokobara wordmark SVG composites unaltered low-centre at 9.5 s, inside the ten-second gate, over the frame where the zip opens on the yellow lining. 'Transit Backpack' names it at 17.6 s. The wordmark returns on the closing card. The mark is placed, never redrawn, recoloured or regenerated.
brand_timeline.spoken: none — the film carries no dialogue and no voice-over, so the name is never said. It is carried visually three ways instead: the supplied wordmark at 9.5 s and again at 28.0 s, the composited product name at 17.6 s, and the product's own unmistakable navy-and-yellow silhouette in every beat.

last_frame: The packed Transit Backpack standing upright on wet sand, three-quarter front, navy body with a finger of yellow lining at the top and both black zip pulls closed, the flat sea behind it; the supplied Mokobara wordmark above and mokobara.com beneath. The product is the last thing on screen.

deviations.from: / / default: the on-screen CTA is voiced in the same words and the brand name is spoken as well as shown (abcd_0021, 0012, ogx_0042)
deviations.brief_clause: The job's standing production constraint — no dialogue or voice-over — together with deliverable_request.motion.from = 'generated'. There is no voice to pair with, so the film pays the debt on the visual channel instead: the wordmark inside ten seconds, the name supered on the performing frame, the pack as the last image, and a designed effects track in which the zip does the work a line would have done.

deviations.from: / / default: set out to be interesting, not funny; no humour unless a brief clause asks, and only from a writer who can write it
deviations.brief_clause: "would be funny that he could keep his arms in the bag and food and so much stuff" — the customer asks for the gag in their own words. The override is taken at minimum dose: one beat, one static shot, no cutaway, no comic music sting, no mugging, and the exaggeration grounded on a stated truth (30L and the front bucket pocket) so the shot still sells capacity if the joke does not land.

deviations.from: default: the aspect is justified by a named shape in the scene, not by the platform alone
deviations.brief_clause: deliverable_request.aspect = "9:16". The aspect is fixed by the customer before any scene exists, and the pack's own LIMIT records that no accepted source treats fixed vertical feed frames. Rather than leave it unjustified, the film gives the long axis a job — sky and open sea opposed against hand, rock and pack at the bottom of every frame — which is a transfer of a landscape-stills claim made by me, not by the source.
